trigger: A change creates or modifies rendered web or mobile UI, user interaction behavior, responsive layout, navigation or focus behavior, accessibility semantics, or browser-only runtime behavior.
exitSignal: Every affected user flow has current browser or app-runtime evidence at relevant viewport and input modes, applicable accessibility checks pass, and any unresolved usability or accessibility limitation is explicit.
evidence: An affected-flow inventory maps changed acceptance criteria to pages, screens, interaction states, viewport classes, and relevant input modes.
Current runtime evidence exercises each changed flow through the real rendered interface, including applicable loading, empty, error, disabled, validation, and success states.
Automated accessibility results cover affected rendered surfaces, and manual evidence covers applicable assistive input, focus, names, announcements, reflow, and motion behavior.
Responsive evidence names tested viewport classes and records overflow, clipping, target size, orientation, and content-reflow outcomes.
Findings identify severity, affected flow, reproduction, and disposition, with accepted limitations visible in final risk and handoff evidence.
